checks: The diagonal is b_i−h_{i−1}−h_i, and the adjacent off-diagonal for edge i is −h_i, including m=3 where the three unordered edges are distinct. The positive-edge graph components therefore give matrix blocks.

Redistributing each node coefficient using the slack yields the asserted square, because s−rs/(r+s)=s²/(r+s), r−rs/(r+s)=r²/(r+s), and the mixed coefficient is −2rs/(r+s). There is no quotient on a zero edge.

Compactness of the unit sphere gives a least Rayleigh vector on each block, and absolute values preserve or lower its quotient. A zero entry in a nonnegative minimizing eigenvector propagates over all strictly negative off-diagonals, so a nonsingleton connected block has a positive minimizing eigenvector. A singleton contributes entry one; its scalar eigenvalue is nonnegative under PSD.

For w>0 the reciprocal sum on a positive edge is 1/h_i. Substituting the explicit charges gives slack (Lw)_i/w_i, so singular blocks cause no loss of finiteness and their budgets are tight. When all h vanish, this simply reduces to b_i≥0.

The square-root substitution covers the entire nonnegative orthant, including its boundary. Replacing x by its absolute value can only decrease the form. Equality in the Gram identity forces each slack term and edge square separately to vanish, which gives s_i/r_i=x_{i+1}/x_i for positive entries of a positive block null vector.

Independently checked h=(1,0,0,0), b=(3,3/2,0,5). The form is (2x₁−x₂)²/2+5x₄², with the singular edge vector (1,2,0,0) giving equality at θ=(1,4,0,0). The reconstruction from w=(1,2,1,1) gives r₁=3/2, s₁=3 and all other edge charges zero. Reducing b₂ to 1 gives form value −2 on that vector. For m=3, h_i=1, b_i=4 gives the cycle sum of squared differences and equality on the all-ones vector.

Proves a three-by-three copositivity test in a mixed-area setting. That test can address the three-node quadratic form at the algebraic level but does not prove the arbitrary cyclic charge equivalence, construct charges, or give the identity for all valid charges.
